Click a node to see where else it is used. Nodes with a badge appear in more than one panel.

Shortcuts & help

Read the board
Click a node
select it — the inspector says where else it is used, and every other usage is ringed
Double-click
go to the next usage. On a node drawn twice in ONE panel, the next place of it; double-press a place you can see to land on THAT one
n / N
next / previous usage, without leaving the keyboard
Click an edge
select the statement; the same statement drawn in another panel is one double-press away
identity / echo
Filters: identity is “this IS the same node”, echo is “the same shape, used elsewhere”
Move around
Drag
pan, from anywhere — a drag that starts on a node still pans
Wheel
zoom around the cursor
f / 0
fit the whole board
Esc
step back out of whatever is on top: a dialog, a menu, a panel filling the view, then the panel that has the keys, then the selection
◀ ▶ or [ ]
step back / forward through the views you have been through · in-app, separate from the browser's own Back/Forward
Panels with more inside
⊞ in a panel's corner
open the panel here, beside its neighbours — nothing else moves. Press it again to close it
⤢ in a panel's corner
the same open, and fill the view with it. Esc gives the view back and leaves the panel open
Click inside an open panel
that panel takes the wheel and the keys — its edge is lit while it has them. Esc hands them back to the board
Ctrl/⌘+click or the corner ⊕
go deeper into what a node contains; Alt as well steps one level instead of all of them
Esc with nothing focused
close every open panel
Search
/
search every node and edge — ↑↓ step the hits, Enter opens one
a b · a+b
AND — every term must match
a/b
OR, binding tighter than AND
(a b)/c
parentheses group, so priority is explicit
Panels
Drag a bar
move the whole card; drop it on another card to zip them together
▾ on the first panel
fold the card away; its ⋮ is the card's menu — hide it, or tick any panel on and off
⋮ on any panel
that panel's own moves, plus Panel controls on the bars and Reset the arrangement
